# TextureRegion

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Graphics` · class

```csharp
public sealed class TextureRegion : ITextureSource
```

Types: [`ITextureSource`](ITextureSource.md)

Represents a rectangular sub-region of a [`Texture`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Texture.md), such as a sprite packed into a texture atlas. Implements [`ITextureSource`](ITextureSource.md) so it can be passed anywhere the framework accepts a textured rectangle.

## Remarks

A `TextureRegion` is a non-owning view of its source texture. It has no lifetime of its own and is not `IDisposable`; the underlying [`Texture`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Texture.md) is owned by whoever created it (typically the atlas that holds the base texture).

[`Bounds`](#bounds) describes the region's logical rectangle in the coordinate space of the underlying texture — the rectangle the sprite occupies from the caller's point of view (matching TexturePacker's `sourceSize`/`spriteSourceSize`). For atlas-packed sprites whose fully-transparent borders were trimmed during packing, the pixels that actually live in the underlying texture may cover only a sub-rectangle of [`Bounds`](#bounds), exposed as [`PackedFrame`](#packedframe) (matching TexturePacker's `frame`).

## Constructors

```csharp
public TextureRegion(ITextureSource source, RectangleInt bounds, RectangleInt? frame = null, ThicknessInt? caps = null, ThicknessInt? outset = null)
```

Types: [`ITextureSource`](ITextureSource.md), [`RectangleInt`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/RectangleInt.md), [`ThicknessInt`](ThicknessInt.md)

Creates a region of the specified source texture.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `source` | The texture this region is a view of. If `source` is itself a `TextureRegion`, the rectangles are in that region's coordinate space and are composed with it, and the result points directly at the underlying texture. |
| `bounds` | The logical (untrimmed) rectangle this region covers, in the source's coordinate space. Must have positive width and height and lie within the source's bounds. Matches TexturePacker's `sourceSize`/`spriteSourceSize`. |
| `frame` | The part of the source holding the sprite's pixels, for a trimmed region, within `bounds`; `null` for all of it. Matches TexturePacker's `frame`. |
| `caps` | 9-slice cap insets in the region's logical coordinate space, or `null` if it isn't a nine-patch. |
| `outset` | How far the region's logical rectangle extends outside its layout bounds (a baked-in drop shadow, for example), or `null` if it doesn't. |

**Throws `ArgumentNullException`:** `source` is `null`.

**Throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`:** `bounds` has non-positive size or doesn't fit within the source's bounds, or it doesn't intersect a trimmed source's frame, or `frame` doesn't lie within the rectangles it must.

Gets the logical (untrimmed) rectangle, within the underlying texture, that this region occupies. Equivalent to TexturePacker's `sourceSize`/`spriteSourceSize`.

### Caps

```csharp
public ThicknessInt? Caps { get; }
```

Types: [`ThicknessInt`](ThicknessInt.md)

Gets the 9-slice cap insets authored for this region, in the region's logical (untrimmed) coordinate space, or `null` when the region is not a nine-patch. Populated by content loaders that understand nine-patch metadata (e.g. TexturePacker's `border` field).

### Outset

```csharp
public ThicknessInt? Outset { get; }
```

Types: [`ThicknessInt`](ThicknessInt.md)

Gets the amount, in logical pixels, that the region's [`Bounds`](#bounds) extends outside its layout (visual) bounds, such as a baked-in drop shadow or glow, or `null` when none was authored. Populated by content loaders from the atlas manifest's `layout` rectangle.

### PackedFrame

```csharp
public RectangleInt PackedFrame { get; }
```

Types: [`RectangleInt`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/RectangleInt.md)

Gets the rectangle within [`Texture`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Texture.md) that contains this region's actual pixels (TexturePacker's `frame`). For a non-trimmed region this equals [`Bounds`](#bounds); for a region whose fully-transparent border was trimmed during atlas packing it is a (possibly smaller) sub-rectangle lying inside [`Bounds`](#bounds). For a region created by [`WithOutset`](#withoutset) it extends outside [`Bounds`](#bounds) by the outset.

## Methods

### WithOutset

```csharp
public TextureRegion WithOutset(ThicknessInt outset)
```

Types: [`ThicknessInt`](ThicknessInt.md)

Creates a view of this region whose logical [`Bounds`](#bounds) is deflated by `outset` while the drawn [`PackedFrame`](#packedframe) is unchanged, so pixels such as a baked-in drop shadow are drawn outside the logical bounds.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `outset` | The amount, in logical pixels, to deflate the logical rectangle by. Must not be negative. |

**Returns:** The new region, or this region when `outset` is zero.

**Throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`:** `outset` has a negative side, or leaves no positive logical size.

This is the inverse of trimming: the frame extends outside the logical rectangle instead of lying inside it. The existing trim-aware draw path offsets the frame accordingly, so there is no additional per-draw cost. Layout (via [`Size`](#size)) uses the visual bounds, excluding the outset.

The returned region is intended for plain sprites. It carries no [`Caps`](#caps) or [`Outset`](#outset); use [`NinePatch`](NinePatch.md)'s outset for nine-patches instead.
